status: ACTIVE EVIDENCE-DERIVED CHANGE BASELINE — CONTENT MIGRATION FROM USER-SUPPLIED FACEBOOK EXTRACTION
business_objective: Create an informative, welcoming and visually distinctive website explaining La Bulle Bleue and APAiL, representing publicly reported activities without overpromising and helping visitors contact the association.
primary_user_intent: Understand La Bulle Bleue, identify the right audience information, explore activities and updates, learn about APAiL, then contact the association through a well-organised multi-page site.
critical_user_journeys: Homepage → La Bulle → audience and session information → contact to confirm
Homepage → actualités → dated highlights → Facebook source
Homepage → APAiL → history and reported solidarity work → contact
functional_requirements: Six static HTML pages with dedicated purposes and a common top navigation/footer
Homepage is a concise orientation page, not the full information archive
Persistent navigation on all pages; active route uses aria-current=page
Keyboard-operable compact navigation; Escape closes only an open menu and restores focus
Every page has French language declaration, one H1, one main landmark, unique title and meta description
Static local page links work without a framework or backend
Preserve source/date caveats for venue, session times, dated posts, historical projects and cited organisations
Email and exact Facebook route remain available in the shared footer
No participant photographs, individual diagnoses, medical outcomes or sensitive-data collection
content_requirements: Identify La Bulle Bleue as an APAiL initiative in Chalon-sur-Saône launched in 2021; identify APAiL as created in 1995
Describe both audience groups and Wednesday 14:30 / Saturday 15:00 with clear source/date and confirmation caveat
Show 30 Rempart Saint-Vincent and garden access via rue Leriche with explicit 11 March 2024 source note and confirmation caveat
Represent games, music, art, cooking, garden, outings, animal mediation and parent meetings
Include selected recent 2026 posts with original dates as past highlights
Describe reported Burkina Faso/Morocco solidarity work as history, not a claim all projects remain active
Name volunteer group Les Bleuettes and list organisations cited in posts as non-exhaustive references
Preserve Facebook and email contact routes
Do not publish participant names, individual diagnoses or medical outcomes

brand.direction: Editorial, understated, human and welcoming; professional local-association identity rather than a generic pastel/illustrated landing-page template.
brand.logo_status: Official transparent PNG supplied by the user at assets/logo final.png; integrated in all six page headers and footers in Loop 010.
brand.palette_status: IMPLEMENTED — the user-uploaded transparent logo was sampled directly in Loop 011. The CSS now uses the extracted navy/cobalt/blue/sky/ice family; pale near-white page surfaces are documented as derived tints.

logo_derived_system.palette: Logo-derived cool blues with icy light surfaces; the former clay/ochre palette has been removed.
logo_derived_system.sampling_method: RGBA source 1052×1024; transparent pixels excluded; alpha-weighted 8-cluster colour analysis on a deterministic sample of 120,000 visible pixels. Reported shares are approximate visible-pixel cluster shares; each hex is the nearest actual source pixel to its cluster centre.

visual_requirements.welcome: One compact welcome and first-contact panel; no duplicated approach / volunteer / first-step sections.

technical.image_hosting: Local repository assets under assets/; no remote image host or third-party image request.

accessibility_target: WCAG 2.2 AA; foundation includes semantics, alt text, dimensions, keyboard navigation, reduced-motion fallback and progressive reveal. Manual screen-reader testing remains outstanding.
success_criteria: Homepage is an orientation page under 9,000 characters.
Detailed topics have separate named pages: La Bulle, activities, actualités, APAiL and contact.
All six pages have identical navigation order and a clear current-page marker.
Every page has unique metadata, one H1 and one main landmark.
All internal page links work and the compact menu is keyboard-operable.
Source-derived facts and operational caveats remain on their appropriate pages.
No participant names or unapproved photographs are published.
Responsive layout declarations cover desktop, tablet and mobile; rendered visual validation is reported separately.
The official transparent logo supplied by the user appears consistently in the header and footer of all six pages.
The homepage and activities page use local documentary photos with meaningful alt text; no identifiable participants are shown in the selected crops.
The final CSS palette is sampled from the official logo, documented as exact hex tokens and used consistently across all six pages.
All six pages use the logo-derived blue palette consistently across backgrounds, text, links, cards, borders, focus and button states; no previous warm clay/ochre accents remain.
business_outcome_hypotheses: Specific activity stories may help families understand the initiative
A richer editorial visual system may feel more approachable
Outcomes require visitor feedback/measurement and are not proven by implementation
